title: places_utils.py and function preprocess_input
body: The example given in README uses Image and it does not call function preprocess input The main Keras documentation however uses image load img where image is imported from keras preprocessing and always calls preprocess input which is imported according to the proper cnn architecture I have seen the function preprocess input defined in places utils py but there is no explicit mention about its use Is it necessary Should we import it and use it as the Keras documentation does

comments.body: places utils py goes along the lines of the previous Keras versions before imagenet utils code was delegated to keras applications submodule and is meant to contain utilities for Places data preprocessing So the answer is yes it is necessary just like the original Keras docs suggest

comments.body: atunick I have rerun the example with the image http places2 csail mit edu imgs demo 6 jpg http places2 csail mit edu imgs demo 6 jpg and the results are the following for the hybrid model PREDICTED SCENE CATEGORIES restaurant eating house eating place eatery folding chair patio terrace food court cafeteria Regarding the other image https user images githubusercontent com 17481462 40858563 adb86a74 65ac 11e8 91ae 2363f9687c3f jpg https user images githubusercontent com 17481462 40858563 adb86a74 65ac 11e8 91ae 2363f9687c3f jpg using the hybrid model I get the following predictions PREDICTED SCENE CATEGORIES seashore coast seacoast sea coast sandbar sand bar swimming trunks bathing trunks maillot tank suit bikini two piece while using the plain VGG16 places365 model results in the following predictions PREDICTED SCENE CATEGORIES desert sand desert road beach coast desert vegetation So clearly both models are working fine As expected for the same image the hybrid version and the original version will come up with different predictions and clearly the provided image contains not only the beach as a place but a person wearing a swimming trunk etc Your problem for getting different results might lie in the fact that your python cache subdir models might contain the weights from the previous version So try deleting all previous weight files and running the scripts again before reporting your new results
